transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I guess… mainly my sleep. It’s been really unreliable. Even when I’m exhausted, I get into bed and just lie there thinking about work forecasts and team issues. Then I wake up around 3 or 4 and can’t really shut my brain off again.
How much does this sleep problem interfere with your daily life—like your mood, work, or relationships?

It’s… starting to matter, I guess. Work feels harder—I second-guess decisions a lot, and pipeline reviews can get pretty tense because of it. And at home I’m just drained. I’m not really as present with my husband as I should be.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot throughout the day, even when you're not at work or thinking about specific problems?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not always one specific thing. My mind just kind of jumps around—like whether we’ll hit launch numbers, or if someone on my team is unhappy, then suddenly it’s the mortgage or a client renewal. Small delays start to feel like they could turn into something bigger.
Do you find that you feel anxious or worried most days, even when there isn’t a specific problem happening at the moment?

Yeah… most days, I think. Even if nothing is actually happening, my mind goes from launch numbers to whether someone on my team might leave, then the mortgage or a client renewal. It’s like any small delay starts feeling bigger than it probably is.
Do you notice any physical symptoms like restlessness, muscle tension, or irritability that seem to go along with these worries?
Yeah… mostly I just feel really wound up. Like I can be home having dinner and still feel like I’m sitting in a pipeline review. My shoulders are tight a lot, even when I’m trying to relax.
Do you often wake up feeling unrefreshed, like you didn’t really get restful sleep, even when you’ve been in bed for a while?

Yeah… pretty often. I’ll go to bed exhausted, but then I’m just lying there replaying forecasts or stuff with my team. And sometimes I wake up around 3 or 4 and can’t really get my brain to shut off again. So even if I’ve been in bed awhile, I don’t feel rested.
Do you have trouble sleeping even on nights when you’re not feeling particularly anxious or worried?

Yeah… I think so. Even when I don’t feel especially worried going to bed, sleep is still kind of unreliable. I’ll be exhausted, but then I end up replaying work stuff anyway, and sometimes I’m up around 3 or 4 and can’t really get my brain to shut back off.
Do you find that your anxiety or worry is especially strong in social situations, like meetings or gatherings, where you might be judged or evaluated by others?
I’m not sure it’s specifically that. Meetings can stress me out, but it doesn’t feel like it’s just because people are judging me. It’s more… I don’t know, just pressure in general.
How long have you been having trouble sleeping like this?
Um… I guess it’s been building for about a year. Since the sales division reorganization, so… maybe thirteen months or so.
Would you say that you feel excessive anxiety or worry on most days, even when there isn’t a clear reason for it?

Yeah… most days, I think. It’ll jump around—like whether we’re going to hit launch numbers, or if someone on my team is unhappy, then the mortgage or a client renewal. Even small delays start feeling like they could turn into something bigger.
Do you feel like you have a hard time controlling the worry, even when you try to focus on something else or tell yourself not to think about it?
Yeah… I do. I’ll tell myself, like, “Brenda, you made the plan, just leave it alone,” but then a few minutes later I’m back in it. I’ll settle one worry and then three more kind of show up.
Do you feel especially anxious or worried in the lead-up to social situations, like meetings or presentations, where you might have to speak or be the center of attention?
I’m not sure it’s specifically that. I mean, presentations aren’t my favorite, but I don’t think the worry is only about being in front of people. It’s more… general, I guess.
Do you ever feel anxious or worried even when there isn’t anything specific going on in your work or personal life that seems to explain it?

Yeah… sometimes there isn’t one clear thing. My mind just starts scanning, I guess—work numbers, someone on my team, the mortgage, a client renewal. Even little delays can feel like they’re going to become a bigger problem.
Do you find that worry or anxious thoughts specifically make it hard for you to fall asleep or cause you to wake up during the night?

Yeah. That’s… honestly a big part of why I’m here. I’ll be exhausted, but once I’m in bed I start replaying forecasts or stuff with my team. And then sometimes I wake up around 3 or 4 and I just can’t get my brain to shut off again.
Do you feel that your worry and trouble sleeping have been causing you significant distress or making it harder to function at work or home?

Yeah… I think so. It’s started to spill over more than I’d like. At work I second-guess decisions a lot, and pipeline reviews get tense because I’m kind of stuck in my head. Then when I get home, I’m just drained… and probably more reactive with my husband than I want to be.
Do you find that your mind is usually racing with worries when you first try to fall asleep, or does it usually start racing after you’ve already fallen asleep?
Both, I guess. When I first lie down, my mind starts going through forecasts or things with my team. And then if I wake up around 3 or 4, it starts again and I can’t really get it to shut off.
Do you feel anxious or have trouble sleeping in different settings, like both at work and at home, or does it seem to be limited to one place or situation?

It’s not really just one place. It’s… kind of everywhere. At work it’s launch numbers or whether someone on my team is unhappy, and then at home it’ll switch to the mortgage or a client renewal. Even small delays start feeling like they could turn into something bigger.
Have you ever had a period where you felt anxious or had trouble sleeping even when everything in your life seemed to be going smoothly and there were no major stressors?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I usually can point to something that feels like a reason, even if it’s small. I haven’t really thought about whether it happens when everything’s actually fine.
